description:
'''''Zhongguo feng''''' ({{zh|p=zhōngguó fēng|t=中國風|s=中国风|l=China style}}), also known as '''''guofeng'' music''' ({{zh|p=guófēng yīnyuè|t=國風音樂|s=国风音乐|l=China-style music}}) or '''[[Chinoiserie]] music''', is a [[music genre|genre]] of [[Chinese popular music]] considered to adopt a more "traditional" style than regular modern popular music, with [[vocal music|vocals]], [[melody]] and [[lyrics]] influenced by [[Chinese opera]] and [[quyi|narrative singing]]. It is different from [[Chinese classical music]] (''[[guoyue]]'') and [[Chinese folk music|folk music]] (''min'ge'') in that, ''Zhongguo feng'' is essentially Western-style contemporary [[pop music]] infused with elements of [[Chinese culture]] and [[Chinese philosophy|philosophy]], and also often with a strong [[musical theme|thematic]] emphasis on [[cultural identity|cultural pride]]; while the latter two focus more on traditional oriental [[instrumental]] [[rhythm]]s and [[singing|vocal performance]].

While [[Mandopop]] singers such as [[Huang An (singer)|Huang An]], [[Sarah Chen]] and [[Tu Honggang]] already gained popularity in [[Mainland China]] and [[Taiwan]] during the 1990s, Taiwanese singer-songwriter [[Jay Chou]] is typically regarded as the first ''Zhongguo feng'' artist to have widespread influence in [[Greater China]]. Following the success of Chou's early works including "Wife" ({{Lang-zh|c=娘子|labels=no}}) and "East Wind Breaks" ({{Lang-zh|t=東風破|labels=no}}), the genre emerged in the C-pop music scene in the early 2000s. Contemporary singers such as [[Phoenix Legend]], [[Li Yugang]], [[Zhou Shen]] and [[Sa Dingding]] are also prominent examples of ''Zhongguo feng'', particularly in the era of [[music streaming service]]s.

[[Gufeng music|''Gufeng'' music]] is a similar but different music genre that is often confused with ''Zhongguo feng'', with ''gufeng'' referring more specifically to modern [[musical composition]]s and ''[[tanci]]''-like songs with similar instrumental and vocal styles of classical music.
